summary: Round r1 (restricted network). A seven-theatre conflict watchlist was built linking conflicts to Nepal's channels (migrant employment, remittances, fuel and shipping routes, aviation hubs). Primary conflict-data leads located: UCDP GED 25.1 (codebook, Zenodo deposit, download centre incl. monthly Candidate Events) and ACLED (Conflict Index and 2026 Watchlist, Middle East monthly overviews January-July 2026, Gulf region hub). The 2026 Middle East escalation flagged unverified by 16B is corroborated at the lead level by independent sources across tiers (Nepal MoFA press statements, IOM DTM, UNCTAD, ACLED), but no event observation has been recorded; all intensity metrics are pending. No values were retrieved.

findings.claim: Q1: Active conflicts in countries hosting Nepali migrant workers - list of countries with UCDP state-based/non-state/one-sided violence events and ACLED severity category, matched against DoFE labour-approval destinations.
findings.note: Requires GED 25.1 (calendar 2024) and UCDP Candidate Events 2025-2026, ACLED Conflict Index (Dec 2024-Nov 2025 window) and DoFE destination list (Nepal FY). Leads 19A-L01..L07; DoFE list from 16B L12/L13.

findings.claim: Q1: Active conflicts on Nepal's supply routes - Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb, Strait of Hormuz, Indian Ocean approaches to Kolkata/Haldia and Visakhapatnam, and air corridors via Gulf hubs.
findings.note: Requires ACLED maritime/coastal event extracts (Yemen, Iran, Gulf littoral) and UNCTAD chokepoint transit data; leads 19A-L09..L13, 19A-L18; 19C route mapping.

findings.claim: Status of the reported 2026 Middle East conflict (flagged unverified by 16B): multiple independent leads were located - ACLED Middle East special issue (March 2026) and monthly overviews (April, May, July 2026), Government of Nepal MoFA press statements and advisories, IOM DTM mobility reports, and UNCTAD Hormuz rapid analysis - describing an escalation beginning late February 2026 involving the United States, Israel and Iran with spillover to GCC states and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Status is corroborated at the lead level only; no event observation has been recorded.
findings.note: Retrieve 19A-L09, L10, L13, L17 and 19C-L05..L07; record dated event observations (onset date, affected countries, current ceasefire/agreement status) before any scenario use. No counts or fatalities taken from snippets.

findings.claim: Conflict-affected destinations with Nepali workers outside the Gulf: Israel, Lebanon, Iraq (incl. Kurdistan Region), and Russia (reports of Nepali nationals recruited into armed forces) - event exposure and worker presence unquantified.
findings.note: Requires ACLED/UCDP country extracts and MoFA consular records; no Russia-specific primary lead was located in r1 (search budget exhausted).

findings.claim: A conflict is 'active' for watchlist purposes if UCDP records at least the UCDP threshold of battle-related deaths for the calendar year, OR ACLED classifies the country in its top severity categories in the latest Conflict Index; the two sources are reported side by side, never merged.
Exposure is defined by overlap with Nepal's channels (migrant employment, remittances, fuel and shipping routes, aviation hubs), not by conflict intensity alone.

data_gaps: UCDP GED annual release ends calendar 2024; 2025-2026 coverage requires UCDP Candidate Events (provisional) or ACLED.
ACLED data exports require registration/terms acceptance; access under platform terms must be confirmed by 00A.
No primary Nepal source located for Nepali nationals in Russian armed forces (MoFA statements expected).
Country-level match of conflict events to Nepali worker locations within destination countries (sub-national) is not available.

WebSearch budget for the session was exhausted during r1 before all lead searches were completed; leads marked 'NOT confirmed by web search' use catalog base URLs or known primary domains and must be verified on fetch.

assumptions.text: UCDP and ACLED differ in event definitions (UCDP: organised violence with fatality threshold; ACLED: includes demonstrations, strategic developments); values are reported separately.
Watchlist inclusion is qualitative until intensity metrics are retrieved.

challenges.text: The 2026 Middle East escalation now has tier-1 (MoFA Nepal) and tier-3 (IOM, UNCTAD) leads in addition to ACLED; recommend upgrading its status from 'unverified report' to 'lead-corroborated, pending retrieval' in the exposure register notes.

S01's trigger is labelled HYPOTHETICAL but a real 2026 event with similar features is lead-corroborated; red team should review whether S01 needs recalibration as a historical-analogue scenario once observations exist.
Escalation per rules: once retrieved, 2026 event observations may change S01 and S10 conclusions.
Russia-related migrant-safety theatre has no catalog source; request MoFA consular statements be added as leads in r2.

uncertainty: High. Watchlist is qualitative; all conflict intensity measures are pending. Event status of 2026 developments rests on lead descriptions, not retrieved documents. UCDP/ACLED coverage and definitions differ.

conflict_watchlist.method: Match UCDP GED/Candidate events and ACLED Conflict Index categories by country and calendar month to (a) DoFE destination countries and (b) route segments from 19C; report UCDP and ACLED separately.
